drivingQuestion: How do an ordinary person, a High Priest and a king differ in bowing during the Amida?
outcomeNote: Two versions of R' Yehoshua ben Levi's teaching are set side by side and neither is decided.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁאָדָם שׁוֹחֶה בָּהֶן: בְּ״אָבוֹת״, תְּחִלָּה וָסוֹף. בַּ״הוֹדָאָה״, תְּחִלָּה וָסוֹף. וְאִם בָּא לָשׁוּחַ בְּסוֹף כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה, וּבִתְחִלַּת כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה — מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁחֶה.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a Tosefta: «These» are the «blessings» in the Amida prayer «in which a person bows: In» the first blessing, the blessing of the «Patriarchs,» one bows «at the beginning and the end; in» the blessing of «thanksgiving,» one bows «at the beginning and the end; and if one seeks to bow at the end of each and every blessing and at the beginning of each and every blessing, they teach him not to bow» so as not to go beyond the ordinance instituted by the Sages.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא: הֶדְיוֹט, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said» that «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of» the tanna «bar Kappara: An ordinary» person «[hedyot],» conducts himself «as we said;» he bows at the beginning and the end of the blessings of Patriarchs and thanksgiving and is admonished if he seeks to bow at the beginning and end of the other blessings.

segments.he: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, בְּסוֹף כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה. וְהַמֶּלֶךְ, תְּחִלַּת כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה וְסוֹף כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה.
segments.en: It is appropriate, though, for «a High Priest» to bow «at the end of each and every blessing; and» for «a king» to bow «at the beginning of each and every blessing and at the end of each and every blessing.» This is because the more lofty one’s status, the more important it is to demonstrate his subservience to God.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֶדְיוֹט, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ. כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, תְּחִלַּת כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה. הַמֶּלֶךְ — כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת שְׁלֹמֹה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וְגוֹ׳ קָם מִלִּפְנֵי מִזְבַּח ה׳ מִכְּרֹעַ עַל בִּרְכָּיו״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani said: It was explained to me» directly «from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi» himself differently: «An ordinary» person, conducts himself «as we said; a High Priest» bows at «the beginning of each and every blessing; the king, once he has bowed» at the beginning of the first blessing, «does not rise» until he concludes the entire prayer, «as it is stated: “And it was that when Solomon finished praying» all of his prayer to the Lord, «he rose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling upon his knees» with his hands spread forth toward the heavens” (I Kings 8:54).

moves.summary: Baraita: one bows in Avot and Hoda'a, beginning and end; one who would bow in every blessing is taught not to.
moves.about: the blessings in which one bows: Avot and Hoda'a, beginning and end; one who would bow in every blessing is taught not to

moves.summary: Bar Kappara (via R' Yehoshua ben Levi and R' Shimon ben Pazi): the baraita's rule is for an ordinary person.
moves.about: the baraita's restriction of bowing to Avot and Hoda'a concerns an ordinary person only; a High Priest bows at the end of every blessing and a king at the beginning and end of every blessing

moves.summary: Continuation: a High Priest bows at the end of every blessing, a king at the beginning and end of every blessing.
moves.about: the baraita's bowing rule applies to an ordinary person; the High Priest and king bow more

moves.summary: R' Yitzchak bar Nachmani reports a different version received directly from R' Yehoshua ben Levi: the High Priest bows at the beginning of each blessing, the king once bowed does not rise.
moves.about: a different version of R' Yehoshua ben Levi's teaching on how the High Priest and king bow

moves.summary: Proof for the king's rule: Solomon rose from kneeling only when he finished praying.
moves.about: Solomon rose from kneeling only when he finished praying
